title: Three bills for the same task: output is what costs, caching is what saves

groups.label: Plan A: one vague line, write freely
groups.text: Prompt: take a look at this ticket, reply to the customer, and write it in detail.
groups.note: Input 900 + output 1600 (example rates: input ¥4/M, output ¥16/M). ¥0.0036 + ¥0.0256 = ¥0.0292 per call; at 100k calls/day ≈ ¥2,920/day, about ¥87,600/month. Cheapest input, priciest bill — the output rate is 4× the input rate, and free-form generation burns output.

groups.label: Plan B: structured prompt, short output
groups.text: Prompt: you are the support agent. Task: answer the ticket. Constraints: stick to the ticket's facts. Output format: JSON only, {"reply": string, "action": enum}, reply at most 80 characters.
groups.note: Input 1500 (the format declaration adds a few hundred tokens — input actually gets pricier) + output 450. ¥0.006 + ¥0.0072 = ¥0.0132 per call; at 100k calls/day ≈ ¥1,320/day, about ¥39,600/month — ¥48,000/month cheaper than A. The lever is generating less, not a cheaper model.

groups.label: Plan C: B plus a cache-stable prefix
groups.text: Prompt: identical to B, but the system block plus the format declaration form a byte-stable prefix that hits the cache on every request.
groups.note: Of the 1500 input tokens, 1200 hit the cache and bill at 1/10 of the input rate (effective input 300 + 1200×0.1 = 420); output 450. ¥0.00168 + ¥0.0072 = ¥0.00888 per call; at 100k calls/day ≈ ¥888/day, about ¥26,640/month — ¥12,960/month cheaper than B and 70% cheaper than A.
